title: Scoped negative result: volume-aware selector batching of complex children
head: dce137e540acd2b689281afe222cd32c0ec1f1ae
body:
An attempted replacement of two equal-rank complex children by one selector-batched call gives a false moment saving if the joined array's volume is omitted. This **scoped negative result** supplies the exact circuit, restoration of arbitrary dirty padding, and the complete volume-weighted budget on a source-pinned pair of rank-2 calls from the accepted #626 `jp8` supplier. **No new κ or supplier is claimed.**

At the accepted supplier's complex exponent, the unweighted `2 C_2 -> C_3 + C_1` comparison gives ratio **0.999786029497691095**. The actual joined array has twice the volume, giving **1.999572058995382190**. Even granting the inverse selector and all routing/frame work for free leaves ratio **1.499003977340941911**. Exact rational enclosures are included.

The note distinguishes the two uniform scaling regimes: a fixed pair uses one selector bit and has the same leading asymptotic moment; a selector slot scaled by `f` requires `2^f` lanes and cannot retain the two-stream volume. A support argument excludes replacing selector correction by monomial routing alone. These are comparisons of the inherited cost bounds, not lower bounds on arbitrary algorithms or a defect claim against production admission.

All new research material is in `research/selector-batching/`, plus one focused CI workflow. The selected record, supplier code, and `upstream/` are unchanged.

```sh
python3 -B research/selector-batching/verify.py
```

Expected: `PASS_SELECTOR_BATCHING_IDENTITIES_AND_VOLUME_OBSTRUCTION`.

Validation completed locally on Python 3.14.6 / macOS:

- 34 full forward/inverse operator cases, **2,776 exact basis columns / 753,568 entries**, including **60 arbitrary dirty-padding columns**. Integer Gaussian butterflies agree with a separate closed-form Kronecker reference.
- Six operator controls and three incomplete-invoice controls rejected; concrete operator counterexamples retained.
- Normal and isolated optimized replays pass. A relocated minimal checkout with a recompressed input gives the same certificate. Changed native input and corrupted expected certificate both fail under `-I -O`.
- `make selected-record-check`, local documentation links and staged whitespace checks pass.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. Assignment seed **22**, complex supplier. The initial review covered 487 open PRs; the pre-submission refresh covered 495 through #675, followed by an immediate check of #676–#678. No pinned sprint issue existed at either check; the local claim records the completed scope. #646/#651 cover the other candidate tasks. This experiment differs from within-array tensor batching, #451's split-residual routing, #665's spectral dilation, and #673's nonlinear dirty echo.

The all-size conclusion relies on the written tensor identity and monotonicity argument, not extrapolation from finite replay. Full supplier/repository-wide replay and Lean were not run locally for this isolated research addition. [Focused Linux CI](https://github.com/g-guthrie/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38343413803) passed on Python 3.11 and 3.14 at the submitted head `dce137e540acd2b689281afe222cd32c0ec1f1ae`. The broader inherited CI is separate and is not claimed complete.

Prepared by **Greer Guthrie** with substantial **OpenAI Codex** assistance. The package credits Kothe, Boukhalfa, eumemic, icekylinx, DreamingOfClouds, Arun and the retained construction lineage; all new material is Apache-2.0.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
